name: Ephesos water-powered stone saw
summary: A late-antique workshop at Ephesos, with a water channel and half-sawn marble blocks, appears to have used water power to drive several saw blades through stone.
description: A late-antique workshop with a water channel and two partly sawn marble blocks, interpreted as water-powered multiple-blade stone sawing.

date.basis: The cited archaeology assigns the installation to the sixth or early seventh century; c.700 is a conservative upper horizon.

events.statement: Partly cut in-situ blocks and the workshop water channel indicate a local productive sawing application.
events.caveats: Crank, wheel support and blade-frame details are competing modern reconstructions; no direct ancestry from Hierapolis or Gerasa is established.

evidence.supports: Two in-situ blocks and water channels show an interpreted saw installation; reconstruction of the drive is contested.
